findings.title: The phone layout does not reflow, so the booking form is mostly off the screen

location.description: the Search button of the Find a boat card, past the right edge on the phone

findings.viewer_experience: A phone visitor must pan sideways to use the page, and the one tool that books a boat is hidden. The navigation stacks in five lines and the text columns are about 9 characters wide.

current.value: page 587 px wide in a 390 px viewport

findings.target: page width equal to the viewport width, no sideways scroll, form in full view
findings.fix_direction: Below about the tablet width, stack the page into one column with the form in full view, and collapse the navigation into a menu or a single row.

closed_when.check: page_width of the phone viewport is 390 or less, and the button box in the phone viewport lies within 0 to 390 px

findings.title: Two starting points compete, and the form's own submit button is styled as the lesser one

location.description: the filled See boats and dates button on the left, against the outlined Search button in the form

findings.viewer_experience: The visitor must stop and work out which button to use, and the filled one skips the base, dates, nights and berths they could fill in beside it.

current.value: one filled button and one outlined button that both appear to start a search

findings.target: one filled primary action per view
findings.fix_direction: Pick one start, usually the prefilled form with its Search button as the single filled primary. Remove the other button or demote it to a text link.
findings.source: Material Design 3, Buttons; NN/g on button emphasis

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees only one filled primary action in each viewport, and no second button that leads to the same result

findings.title: The headline is weaker than the paragraph under it, and the claim that sets this company apart sits at the end of that paragraph

location.description: the h1 above the lead paragraph

findings.viewer_experience: The headline looks smaller than its own text, nothing reads as the title, and the reason to book direct comes last.
findings.target: headline the largest and darkest text on the page, a clear step above the lead, contrast of at least 4.5:1, three or four type sizes with real gaps, and the direct-booking claim in the first read
findings.fix_direction: Make the headline the largest and darkest text, a clear step above the lead, and drop the sizes to three or four with real gaps. Move the direct-booking claim forward, for example by folding the existing words 'book it here with the boatyard that keeps it, no fee on top' into the headline or a line right under it.
findings.source: Bringhurst 3.1.1; Dair, Design with Type, chapters 8 and 9; Tschichold

closed_when.check: h1 font_size is larger than p.lead font_size, and h1 contrast is 4.5 or more, in the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports

findings.title: There is no picture of a boat or the canal

location.description: the large empty middle of the hero, beside the form

findings.viewer_experience: People buy a week on a narrowboat as a holiday and want to see the boat and the water; the headline carries the whole idea alone.

current.value: only a form and a list, no image

findings.target: one real photograph of the company's own boats or canal in the hero beside the form
findings.fix_direction: Add one real photograph of the company's own boats or canal, set into the hero beside the form. The maker must supply the photograph; a stock shot would not do the same job.

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees a real photograph of a boat or the canal in the hero of the desktop and widescreen views

findings.title: The route details are gray at 4.46:1, just under the minimum

location.description: the route details such as 7 nights, 38 locks

findings.viewer_experience: The details are slightly too faint for low-vision readers.
findings.fix_direction: Darken the route details to clear 4.5:1.

closed_when.check: contrast of ul > li > span:nth-of-type(2) in the desktop, phone, tablet and widescreen viewports is 4.5 or more

findings.title: 38 locks has no point of reference for a first-time hirer

location.description: the 38 locks count in the first route

findings.viewer_experience: A first-time hirer cannot tell whether 38 locks is a gentle week or hard work.

current.value: a bare lock count with no meaning given

findings.target: the lock count says what it means for the hirer
findings.fix_direction: Tell the hirer what the count means for them. This needs a fact only the company has, such as how hard or gentle the week is; the maker must supply it.

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees that the route details say what the lock count means for the hirer, in words from the company

findings.title: Routes from Hartwell Junction depends on the Base field but sits far from it

location.description: the Routes from Hartwell Junction heading, about 280 px below the hero

findings.viewer_experience: It reads as a separate section and will not obviously change when the base changes.

current.value: about 280 px below the hero, far from the Base field

findings.target: the routes section is near the Base field or visibly tied to it
findings.fix_direction: Move it nearer the form, or tie it to the form visibly.

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees the routes section near the form or visibly tied to the Base field in the desktop and widescreen views

findings.title: On widescreen the content is pinned to the two side edges with about 850 px of empty space between

location.description: the hero text on the left and the form card on the right

findings.viewer_experience: The eye must cross the whole screen from the headline to the form.

current.value: about 850 px of empty space between the two columns

findings.fix_direction: Cap the content width so the two columns sit together.

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees the hero text and the form close together in the widescreen view, with no wide empty gap between them

findings.title: On the phone, route details split a number from its unit

location.description: the 4 nights, 12 / locks detail of the second route

findings.viewer_experience: The number 12 sits on one line and its unit locks on the next, as does 61 and locks.
findings.target: each number stays on the same line as its unit
findings.fix_direction: Keep the number and its unit together.

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees no number split from its unit in the route details in the phone view

findings.title: Start date looks like a plain text field with no calendar cue

location.description: the Start date input in the Find a boat card

findings.viewer_experience: If it does not open a date picker, visitors can type dates the system cannot read.

current.value: looks like a plain text field

findings.target: the field shows that it is a date picker
findings.fix_direction: Show that it is a date picker.

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees a cue on the Start date field that it opens a date picker

findings.title: The borders of the input and select fields look pale against the white card

location.description: the borders of the input and select fields in the Find a boat card

findings.viewer_experience: Pale field borders are hard to see for low-vision readers.
findings.target: border contrast of at least 3:1 against the card
findings.fix_direction: Measure the borders against 3:1, and darken them if they fall short.

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees field borders that stand clear of the white card in every viewport

findings.title: On the tablet the lead paragraph ends with hire. alone on its last line

location.description: the last line of the lead paragraph on the tablet

findings.viewer_experience: A single word alone on the last line looks unfinished.
findings.target: no one-word last line in the lead paragraph
findings.fix_direction: Rebalance the lines so the last line holds more than one word.

closed_when.check: a fresh critic sees no one-word last line in the lead paragraph in the tablet view
